summary: The user relies entirely on Unannounced Meals (UAM) without carbohydrate logging while taking a GLP-1 medication. Dangerously high safety limits (Max IOB of 25 U and Max Basal of 12 U/h) are allowing the system to over-correct prolonged post-meal spikes, directly resulting in severe evening and overnight hypoglycemia.

analysis_steps.evidence: CGM coverage is 98.7% with 3995 entries. Profile is authoritative. Zero carbs are logged in the 14-day telemetry.
analysis_steps.findings: Telemetry is robust for glucose and loop actions, but the complete absence of carbohydrate data obscures true meal onsets and actual insulin-to-carb mismatches. GLP-1 usage is noted.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Missing carbohydrate entries prevent mathematical validation of Carb Ratios and meal absorption times.

analysis_steps.evidence: Time Below Range is 5.1%. Severe hypoglycemia is concentrated in the evening and overnight (e.g., 15.3% TBR at 19:00, 18.5% at 01:00). Glucose extremes reach 41 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.findings: There is a critical safety risk due to severe and prolonged hypoglycemia from the late afternoon through the night. No parameter changes should increase insulin delivery during these windows.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Cannot definitively isolate whether night lows are driven by aggressive targets or lingering insulin from daytime over-corrections without carb data.

analysis_steps.evidence: Target segments are set to 90 mg/dL at 23:00 and 00:00. Average glucose drops significantly into the low 90s and 80s during these hours with high TBR.
analysis_steps.findings: The 90 mg/dL target overnight provides zero safety buffer against lingering insulin and is contributing to the high rate of hypoglycemia. It must be relaxed.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Fasting validation is obscured by the massive evening IOB carryover.

analysis_steps.evidence: ISF is flat at 56 mg/dL/U. DIA is 10 hours. Carb Ratios range from 10.5 to 13.2 g/U but zero carbs are logged.
analysis_steps.findings: A flat ISF coupled with 100% unannounced meals forces the system into a purely reactive state. The 10-hour DIA extends the tracking of these massive UAM corrections deep into the evening, contributing to lows.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Without carb inputs, assessing exact CR accuracy or isolated ISF performance is impossible.

analysis_steps.evidence: UAM is enabled, SMB always enabled, and SMB interval is 3 minutes. Zero logged carbs indicate UAM is the sole meal strategy.
analysis_steps.findings: Because no carbs are logged, UAM triggers frequently (every 3 minutes) during post-meal rises. Delayed gastric emptying from the GLP-1 stretches these rises, causing UAM to over-deploy insulin for prolonged periods in the afternoon.

analysis_steps.evidence: Max IOB is 25 U and Max Basal is 12 U/h. The user's total 14-day insulin is 275.95 U (~19.7 U/day). Dynamic ISF is active and drives sensitivity down to ~39.9 mg/dL/U during highs.
analysis_steps.findings: A critical safety limit mismatch exists. A Max IOB of 25 U exceeds the user's entire Total Daily Dose. This completely removes the algorithm's safety ceiling, allowing Dynamic ISF and UAM to stack catastrophic amounts of insulin during delayed GLP-1 meal spikes.

analysis_steps.evidence: Zero carb treatment entries. All therapy response windows are labeled Correction Bolus. No declared meal strategies.
analysis_steps.findings: The user employs a strictly reactive, zero-logging approach. Relying solely on closed-loop corrections without prebolusing while on a GLP-1 guarantees massive delayed insulin stacking.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: True meal timing and sizing are entirely unknown.

analysis_steps.evidence: Extended carbs are not used (0 entries).
analysis_steps.findings: E-carbs are not utilized. UAM lacks the ability to anticipate the extended tail of GLP-1 delayed meals, heavily compounding the delayed-insulin crash cycle.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Actual duration of meal absorption cannot be modeled without carb inputs.

analysis_steps.evidence: Total synthesis of Checkpoints 1-3 and data package.
analysis_steps.findings: The root cause of the severe overnight hypoglycemia is the combination of delayed GLP-1 meal absorption, a 100% UAM strategy, and dangerously absent safety limits (Max IOB 25 U). The algorithm sees a prolonged afternoon high, uses Dynamic ISF to strengthen delivery, and stacks massive amounts of insulin unchecked. This wall of IOB crashes the user overnight into the tight 90 mg/dL targets.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Carb logging is required to fix underlying CR or basal rates.

strengths: Excellent CGM coverage and adherence at 98.7% uptime.
Consistent use of AAPS notes to log GLP-1 medication administration times and site changes.
issues: Critical hypoglycemia occurring from late afternoon through the night, with extremes down to 41 mg/dL.
Max IOB (25 U) exceeds the user's Total Daily Dose (~20 U), completely neutralizing its function as a safety ceiling.
Zero carbohydrate logging forces the loop to guess the size and duration of GLP-1 delayed meals, leading to massive insulin stacking.
A 90 mg/dL overnight target provides zero safety buffer against lingering afternoon insulin.

recommendations.title: Restrict Max IOB and Max Basal
recommendations.description: The current safety limits are dangerously loose. Max IOB should typically be 30-50% of the Total Daily Dose to prevent the loop from over-stacking insulin during unannounced meal spikes.

recommendations.title: Raise Nighttime Targets
recommendations.description: A target of 90 mg/dL provides no buffer when the system is aggressively fighting delayed spikes. Raising it helps the loop suspend delivery sooner as glucose drops.

recommendations.title: Temporarily Log Carbohydrates
recommendations.description: To safely adjust Carb Ratios or ISF for the GLP-1 delayed absorption, the system (and any future analysis) needs to see when meals are eaten and roughly how large they are.

profile_recommendation.rationale: The 90 mg/dL target leaves no room for error when lingering daytime IOB stacks into the evening, contributing directly to severe overnight hypoglycemia.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Monitor overnight glucose for 3-5 days after raising the target and restricting max IOB to ensure the severe hypoglycemia resolves.
profile_recommendation.recommendation: Raise the 23:00 and 00:00 targets from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL.

meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Zero logging combined with delayed gastric emptying from GLP-1 medication forces AAPS to over-deploy insulin dynamically. Logging carbs will reveal the true absorption delay and prevent the loop from guessing.
meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Temporarily log estimated carbohydrates and true meal times while continuing to rely on UAM and Dynamic ISF.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log carbohydrates for 3-5 days to accurately correlate afternoon glucose rises with actual meal ingestion.

implementation_steps: Address the critical safety risk first: Reduce max_iob_units to approximately 6 U and max_basal_u_per_hour to 3 U/h.
Raise the 23:00 and 00:00 targets from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL to provide a larger safety margin against overnight hypoglycemia.
Begin logging carbohydrate estimates and meal times for 3-5 days to properly assess GLP-1 absorption delays before making any changes to basal rates or Carb Ratios.
education: Max IOB (Insulin on Board) is a critical safety limit. It should typically be set to roughly 30-50% of your Total Daily Dose (TDD). A value higher than the TDD completely removes the algorithm's safety ceiling.

GLP-1 medications significantly delay gastric emptying. The glucose rise from a meal may not peak until several hours later, which can confuse reactive systems like Unannounced Meals (UAM) into heavily stacking insulin.

A target of 90 mg/dL is very aggressive. When insulin is still heavily active from earlier afternoon corrections, having a slightly higher target (e.g., 100 mg/dL) helps the algorithm suspend basal delivery sooner to prevent lows.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely.
The current Max IOB setting of 25 U is extremely dangerous for a user with a ~20 U Total Daily Dose. Address this immediately before altering any other insulin delivery settings.
